packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, one packet per session, prompt and images only (reader brief of PR #76/#77); repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response; reread of packets whose first readings were written after the session's image limit had removed earlier images
text:
packet-09 -- unverified image reading (blind; no identification seen in context; nothing done beyond the brief's rules except making crops)

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview of face A)
- Two separate parchment strips on black ground with colour chart and ruler.
- Left strip (~8 x 5.5 cm): text is UPSIDE DOWN in the photograph (rotated 180 deg). About 9 lines of a single column survive, cropped at the top (as photographed) and on one side; a blank area with stain/damage and a loose thread on the right. A red vertical ruling line is visible near the text edge; small red marks at the line ends.
- Right strip (~11 x 7 cm with a tab extending below): text upright. Single column, ~10 lines on the main piece plus ~4 lines on the lower tab. Red ruling lines visible (horizontal at top, vertical at right of text). Right-hand part of strip is blank (margin), stained brown, with holes; modern pencil shelfmark note in margin ("Stams, STA ... ").
- Script: small Gothic textualis bookhand in brown ink, heavy abbreviation. Red touches (initial strokes/rubrication) at some line beginnings and a red letter at right on the tab.
- Interpretation (tentative): margin strips from a single-column (or wide column) book; no visible glosses.

IMAGE-002 (left strip, native tile). The photograph shows this strip upside down; I rotated it 180 deg (crops 002-rot-top.jpg, 002-rot-bot.jpg) and number lines 1-8 from the top of the ROTATED (reading-upright) view; line 1 here is the lowest line in the unrotated image-002, line 8 the topmost. Red horizontal ruling above line 1 (upright view). Text is cut at the right edge (upright view) after the last letters given; left edge appears to be near the line starts (beginnings are complete or nearly so). The blank right portion of the unrotated tile (= left in upright view) carries a red vertical ruling and a red flourished mark near line 1.
Script: Gothic bookhand with short ascenders; q with stroke, superscript abbreviations; I give abbreviations as seen with tentative expansions.

LAYOUT SURVEY, FACE B (image-005 overview): the same two strips turned over, held flat by two clear plastic spatulas. Left strip again shows text UPSIDE DOWN (~9 lines), with a red letter/mark at line starts near the blank damaged end; blank end on the left as photographed. Right strip: text upright, ~10 lines, with red marginal sigla (e.g. "de", "a") in the left margin and red touches on some lines; modern pencil note "Stams, STA, Fg. 146 Av" on the blank left part. Lower tab carries a large red initial O (with a red-outlined decorated bowl) followed by small capitals/brown text "[.]ENDE?/[...]" and a line below ("s[.]agul[.]"?). Text block of the right strip is on the RIGHT of the blank area on this face (mirror of face A), consistent with the same leaf seen from the other side.

Right of the text (upright view): red vertical ruling with red marginal notes "a" / "a[.]" / "a[.]" (sigla like those on face A) and a red flourish; then the blank damaged end of the strip with the modern pencil note "Stams, STA, Fg. 146 C?v". LIMITATIONS / SUMMARY
- All 8 images were viewed; no image-limit removal occurred.
- Both strips are narrow cuttings; every line is cut on at least one side. Face A left strip and face B left strip are photographed upside down; line numbers for them refer to my 180-degree-rotated view.
- Face A right strip: lines R-L1..R-L10 + tab T1-T5 are the most connected text. Words in red underline (R-L1 "sustinui te d(omi)ne"; face B "ua ap(u)d te", "Spe-", "uia ap(u)d d. mia") look like quoted lemmata with commentary around them (tentative interpretation). Red marginal "ac"/"c" sigla recur on both faces; their meaning is not determined from the images.
- Weak areas: face B right strip L7-L11 second halves (faint, abraded); face A tab T2; face A left strip L3 middle; face B left strip L2 end, L5-L6 middle. Ultraviolet/enhanced images of face B right strip lower half would help.
- No identification of the text was in my context; I did not attempt one. Nothing done beyond the brief except crops saved under responses-rerun/crops/packet-09/.
